prerequisites: FUNDAMENTALS OF MATHEMATICS AND PHYSICS WHICH CAN BE ACQUIRED AT SECONDARY SCHOOL LEVEL

learning_outcomes.text: Critical knowledge of the chemical and chemical-physical foundations necessary to interpret the behavior and transformations of the subject in relation to the main technologies and engineering problems.
Knowledge of the structure of atoms and ability to understand the types of chemical bonds and the resulting molecules, with related chemical and physical properties.
Knowledge of the interactions between atoms and between molecules to understand the various states of aggregation of matter (solid, liquid, gas) and their phase transitions.
Knowledge of redox reactions in ionic environment with limiting reagent.
Knowledge of physical equilibria and state diagrams, homogeneous chemical equilibria in the gas phase and ionic equilibria in aqueous solution.
Knowledge of ideal solutions and colligative properties.
Knowledge of galvanic cells powered by simple spontaneous redox reactions.
Ability to perform calculations related to mass and charge balances in redox reactions.
Ability to predict the direction in which a chemical equilibrium process evolves depending on the effect that external parameters have on the system.
Ability to evaluate the pH of aqueous solutions of acids or bases.
Ability to evaluate the molecular mass of non-volatile solutes in dilute solutions, through the use of colligative properties.
Ability to calculate the electromotive force of galvanic cells and to write the spontaneous direction of the redox reactions that feed them.
The student will be able to evaluate independently: the validity and approximation limits of the interpretative models of the physical and chemical behavior of matter, depending on the structure.

The student will be able to evaluate independently: the areas of use of the fundamental principles of chemistry to understand the criteria that regulate the design and production of substances in relation to their applications.

The student will be able to support conversations on issues related to the chemical fundamentals of technologies by making use of adequate scientific terminology, and the tools of mathematical and graphic representation of the main phenomena described.

syllabus_topics: MATTER AND ENERGY. STRUCTURE OF ATOMS AND ELECTRONIC CONFIGURATIONS. THE PERIODIC SYSTEM.
THE CHEMICAL BOND: ENERGIES AND FORCES OF BONDS. STRONG TIES. STRONG BOND THEORIES: LEWIS, VALENCE BOND, MOLECULAR ORBITALS.
HYBRIDIZATION OF ATOMIC ORBITALS. RESONANCE. MOLECULAR GEOMETRIES
WEAK INTERACTIONS BETWEEN MOLECULES: DIPOLE-DIPOLE, HYDROGEN, VAN DER WAALS.
AMOUNT. MINIMAL AND MOLECULAR FORMULAS. PERCENTAGES IN MASS OF THE ELEMENTS IN THE COMPOUNDS.
OXIDATION STATES. REDOX REACTIONS IN NEUTRAL AND IONIC ENVIRONMENT.
STATES OF MATTER: SOLIDS; GAS; LIQUIDS.
SOLUTIONS AND THEIR PROPERTIES. COLLIGATIVE PROPERTIES. HOMOGENEOUS CHEMICAL EQUILIBRIA IN THE GAS PHASE. IONIC EQUILIBRIA IN AQUEOUS SOLUTION: ACIDS AND BASES.
ELECTROCHEMISTRY. THE BATTERIES. NERNST EQUATION. CALCULATION OF THE F.E.M. OF A PILE AND DETERMINATION OF THE SPONTANEOUS DIRECTION OF THE REDOX REACTION THAT FEEDS IT.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test preparatory to an oral interview. The written test covers stoichiometry exercises. The oral exam aims to fill any gaps from the written test and verify theoretical knowledge. Two partial tests can be taken during the course, each weighing 50% on the overall grade. If the combined partial test score is higher than 18/30, the student is exempt from the written test for the examination session following the teaching session. The final grade, expressed in thirtieths with possible praise, will depend on the global maturity acquired on the course contents and will not be averaged with the written test score.
